dosing.source_quote: Exposure was modeled as a generic input to the plasma compartment (designated as “IV” in Figures 1 and 2) as contributions of PFAA exposure from different exposure routes are not well understood (Fromme et al. 2009).

Exposure was modeled as a generic input to the plasma compartment (designated as “IV” in Figures 1 and 2) as contributions of PFAA exposure from different exposure routes are not well understood (Fromme et al. 2009).

For PFOA, sensitivity analysis was performed assuming an estimated maternal exposure of 1.9e-4 ug/kg BW/day for both gestation and lactation; for PFOS, the analysis was performed assuming an estimated maternal exposure of 4.0e-4 ug/kg BW/day for both the gestation and lactation models.
For PFOA exposure during pregnancy, estimated maternal exposures ranged from 1.1e−04 to 6.9e−04 ug/kg BW/day, and for PFOS, estimated maternal exposures ranged from 1.9e−04 to 4.4e−03 ug/kg BW/day.
For PFOA during lactation, estimated exposures ranged from 1.1e−04 to 2.8e−04 ug/kg BW/day.
PFOS was detected in all studies in plasma or milk, and estimated maternal PFOS exposures during lactation ranged from 3.5e−04 to 2.3e−03 ug/kg BW/day.
The reported concentrations for PFOA in drinking water were used (3.55 ppb for Little Hocking)(Emmett et al. 2006) and 0.519 ppb for Arnsberg (Holzer et al. 2008).
